title.en: What the data can and cannot show
title.es: Lo que los datos pueden y no pueden demostrar

es: Distinguir lo que un estudio demuestra de lo que solo sugiere, detectar sus límites (muestra, datos autodeclarados, factores ocultos) y juzgar qué conclusiones están justificadas al escuchar o leer una reseña.

teaching.en: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher, yet the authors stop short of claiming a causal link.
teaching.es: El estudio sugiere que los adolescentes que duermen más sacan mejores notas, pero los autores no llegan a afirmar una relación causal.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggests es un verbo cauto: apunta a una relación; stop short of + -ing marca que los autores no dan el paso siguiente.
segments: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher,
yet the authors stop short of claiming a causal link.
teaching.audioText: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher, yet the authors stop short of claiming a causal link.

teaching.en: A strong correlation does not demonstrate that one thing causes another, because a third factor may explain both.
teaching.es: Una correlación fuerte no demuestra que una cosa cause la otra, porque un tercer factor puede explicar ambas.
teaching.explanationEs: Demonstrate es un verbo fuerte que exige pruebas de causa; una correlación solo muestra que dos datos van juntos.
segments: A strong correlation does not demonstrate that one thing
causes another, because a third factor may explain both.
teaching.audioText: A strong correlation does not demonstrate that one thing causes another, because a third factor may explain both.

teaching.en: Because the sleep hours were self-reported, the authors cannot rule out that some pupils exaggerated, so the figures may be biased.
teaching.es: Como las horas de sueño eran autodeclaradas, los autores no pueden descartar que algunos alumnos exageraran, así que las cifras pueden estar sesgadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Rule out + that + oración significa «descartar»; biased indica que el método inclina el resultado.
segments: Because the sleep hours were self-reported, the authors cannot rule out
that some pupils exaggerated, so the figures may be biased.
teaching.audioText: Because the sleep hours were self-reported, the authors cannot rule out that some pupils exaggerated, so the figures may be biased.

teaching.en: A key limitation is that only one school took part, so the conclusions may not be justified beyond it.
teaching.es: Una limitación clave es que solo participó una escuela, así que las conclusiones pueden no estar justificadas fuera de ella.
teaching.explanationEs: Justified aplicado a una conclusión indica que los datos la sostienen; beyond it = más allá de esa escuela.
segments: A key limitation is that only one school took part,
so the conclusions may not be justified beyond it.
teaching.audioText: A key limitation is that only one school took part, so the conclusions may not be justified beyond it.

teaching.en: Even a large sample cannot warrant a sweeping claim when no comparison group exists, since other causes remain possible.
teaching.es: Ni siquiera una muestra grande puede justificar una afirmación demasiado general si no hay grupo de comparación, pues otras causas siguen siendo posibles.
teaching.explanationEs: Warrant + afirmación = justificarla; un sweeping claim abarca más de lo que los datos pueden respaldar.
segments: Even a large sample cannot warrant a sweeping claim when
no comparison group exists, since other causes remain possible.
teaching.audioText: Even a large sample cannot warrant a sweeping claim when no comparison group exists, since other causes remain possible.

teaching.en: Headlines often overstate a claim that the researchers made cautiously, and robust evidence is rarely as tidy as the headline suggests.
teaching.es: Los titulares suelen exagerar una afirmación que los investigadores hicieron con cautela, y las pruebas sólidas rara vez son tan limpias como sugiere el titular.
teaching.explanationEs: Overstate a claim = presentarla más fuerte de lo que los datos permiten; robust evidence exige muestra amplia y comparación.
segments: Headlines often overstate a claim that the researchers made cautiously, and
robust evidence is rarely as tidy as the headline suggests.
teaching.audioText: Headlines often overstate a claim that the researchers made cautiously, and robust evidence is rarely as tidy as the headline suggests.

prompt.es: Elige el verbo que mantiene la afirmación dentro de lo que muestran los datos.

choices.text: proves
guarantees
suggests

feedback.es: Sin grupo de comparación y con voluntarios, el verbo adecuado es cauto: suggests; proves y guarantees prometen más de lo que hay.

hint.es: Piensa qué verbo deja abierta la posibilidad de otras causas.

origin.text: The trial had no comparison group, and the results held only for volunteers. The authors write: This study ___ that light exercise may help people to sleep.

prompt.es: Completa: «La correlación no demuestra que una cosa cause la otra.»

feedback.es: Dos datos que suben juntos muestran una correlation; un tercer factor (el calor) puede explicar ambos.

hint.es: Sustantivo que significa que dos datos van juntos sin que uno cause el otro.

origin.text: Ice-cream sales and beach visits rise together, but the ___ between them does not demonstrate that one causes the other; the hot weather explains both.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una reseña con el problema que revela.

pairs: All the volunteers came from one firm.
Nobody was followed over several years.
The paper names a third factor.

feedback.es: Cada frase señala un tipo distinto de límite: muestra, origen del dato, falta de seguimiento o causa alternativa.

hint.es: Pregúntate qué no puede afirmarse a partir de cada frase.

pairs: All the volunteers came from one firm.
Nobody was followed over several years.
The paper names a third factor.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué significa que el resultado sea «tentative, not conclusive».

choices.text: It hints at a possible benefit without settling whether the desks cause it.
It means the desks do reduce pain, although nobody has measured how much.
It shows that the survey was carried out carelessly.

feedback.es: Tentative indica una pista provisional; not conclusive, que no zanja la cuestión: los escritorios pudieron comprarse precisamente donde ya había dolor, así que no se sabe si reducen el dolor ni cuánto.

origin.audio: The authors of a large survey found that people who use standing desks report less back pain. However, the desks were bought by companies that had already noticed staff complaints, so the people with desks may have been the ones in pain to begin with. The authors therefore call their result tentative, not conclusive.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conclusión está justificada por este ensayo?

choices.text: The tablet improved sleep, as the comparison with the group that took nothing shows.
The tablet group reported sleeping better, though their own hopes may have played a part.
The tablet has no effect, since a sample of sixty is far too small.

feedback.es: Como todos sabían qué tomaban, sus propias esperanzas pueden explicar parte del resultado; ni se puede atribuir la mejora a la pastilla ni descartar su efecto solo por el tamaño de la muestra.

origin.text: In a trial, sixty volunteers who took a daily tablet for a month said they slept better, while sixty who took nothing reported no change. Everyone knew which group they were in.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una correlación fuerte no puede justificar una afirmación de causa.»

answer.text: A strong correlation cannot justify a claim of cause

feedback.es: Cannot justify + afirmación recuerda que la relación entre datos no equivale a causa.

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige la conclusión que los datos justifican.

choices.text: The study demonstrates that caffeine improves attention in office workers.
Making fewer mistakes leads people to drink more coffee at work.
Workers in this firm who drink a lot of coffee tend to make fewer errors.

feedback.es: Solo se puede afirmar la correlación observada en esa empresa; que la cafeína mejore la atención o que la relación vaya en sentido contrario son hipótesis que los propios autores dejan abiertas.

origin.audio: A new study of nine hundred office workers reports that people who drink three or more cups of coffee a day make fewer errors. The authors found a clear correlation, but they did not assign anyone to drink coffee: workers simply described their own habits in a questionnaire. The authors suggest that caffeine may improve attention, yet they concede that more alert people might simply drink more coffee. They also note that every worker came from a single insurance firm. A journalist summarised the paper under the headline Coffee Cuts Mistakes, which the lead author called slightly stronger than the evidence allows.

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige la actitud de la autora principal ante el titular.

choices.text: She accepts it as broadly fair but thinks it is a little too confident.
She thinks it is too cautious for a result that the evidence fully supports.
She rejects it as a distortion that has nothing to do with the paper.

feedback.es: La autora no rechaza el titular ni lo aplaude: lo considera algo más rotundo de lo que permiten los datos («slightly stronger»), es decir, razonable pero demasiado seguro.

origin.audio: A new study of nine hundred office workers reports that people who drink three or more cups of coffee a day make fewer errors. The authors found a clear correlation, but they did not assign anyone to drink coffee: workers simply described their own habits in a questionnaire. The authors suggest that caffeine may improve attention, yet they concede that more alert people might simply drink more coffee. They also note that every worker came from a single insurance firm. A journalist summarised the paper under the headline Coffee Cuts Mistakes, which the lead author called slightly stronger than the evidence allows.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los datos no justifican la afirmación de que la dieta causó la mejora.»

feedback.es: Do not warrant the claim significa que los datos no bastan para sostener esa conclusión.

origin.text: The participants chose their own diets, and no group was followed over time. The data therefore do not ___ the claim that the diet itself caused the improvement.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El estudio no puede descartar que los participantes exageraran.»

answer.text: The study cannot rule out that participants exaggerated

feedback.es: Rule out + that + oración expresa que una explicación alternativa sigue siendo posible.

prompt.es: ¿En qué se diferencia la postura del comunicado de prensa de la del artículo científico?

choices.text: The paper goes further, since it shows that reading alone explains the gap.
The paper is more cautious, because other factors could also explain the link.
The paper is more cautious, but only because its sample was much smaller.

feedback.es: El artículo reconoce otros factores que podrían explicar la relación; no va más lejos que el comunicado ni su cautela se debe al tamaño de la muestra, que no se menciona.

origin.text: Press release: Our results show that children who read every night have larger vocabularies. The paper itself is more careful: it notes that families who read together also talk more, own more books and have more time, so the effect of reading alone cannot be separated out.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un estudio pequeño rara vez ofrece pruebas sólidas.»

feedback.es: Robust evidence es la colocación habitual para pruebas que resisten la repetición.

origin.text: One small study, however carefully done, rarely provides robust ___; it needs to be repeated by other teams before anyone can rely on it.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere mostrar Leo con su comentario.

choices.text: Healthier people may take better care of the pets that they keep.
Sara should have checked how the survey defined a pet.
Something else could explain the link between pets and long life.

feedback.es: Leo propone una explicación alternativa (la salud y el dinero) que podría explicar el dato; no habla de que los sanos cuiden mejor a sus mascotas ni critica cómo Sara leyó la encuesta.

origin.audio: Sara read that people who own pets live longer. Leo pointed out that healthier, wealthier people may be more likely to keep pets, so the survey might be measuring health rather than pets. Sara admitted that she had not thought of that and asked whether the article mentioned it.
